bg-3Rlt.title: Road lines: thin
bg-3Rlt.summary: Road lines are usually thin. This helps tell it from Romania, where they are much thicker.

differs.how: Romanian road lines are much thicker

bg-4ipy.title: Google car: dead winter look, March-April
bg-4ipy.summary: Most older Gen 3 coverage was taken in March and April, so it looks grey and lifeless. Hungary and Czechia have lots of this too, and some summer Gen 3 exists.

bg-5asz.title: Pole: three large hook insulators, alternating
bg-5asz.summary: A pole top with three large insulators shaped like upward hooks, alternating sides. Probably unique to this country. Some tops have them facing down.

bg-7hxS.title: Sign: white street name with two red strips
bg-7hxS.summary: White street signs with two red strips, one along the bottom and one across part of the top. They appear in the capital, which also has other sign types.

bg-A9Bj.title: Phone numbers: area codes by first digit
bg-A9Bj.summary: Area codes are one of the best ways to guess the region in city rounds. They are ordered by first digit, so learning those gets you far. Codes in brackets on the map spill over from a neighbouring province, and codes beside a dot belong to the province capital only.

bg-AKrj.title: Houses: orange tiled roofs, mortar patches
bg-AKrj.summary: Most houses have orange tiled roofs with visible patches of mortar along the corner tiles. The roofs often look poorly built, with uneven tiles and mortar.

bg-AxEF.title: Language: Cyrillic, often with Latin too
bg-AxEF.summary: Mostly Cyrillic script, though many signs also have Latin letters. The letter Ъ exists only in Bulgarian and Russian, and is rare in Russian.

bg-BUpU.title: Google car: red Gen 4, with or without antenna
bg-BUpU.summary: A red Gen 4 car, mostly in central and southeastern parts. It can have an antenna or not.

bg-BcFd.title: Landscape: mountain ranges split flat and
bg-BcFd.summary: A mountain chain splits the country in two: flat land to its north up to Romania. A second range starting near the capital runs southeast to Greece and has the highest peaks. Between them is the second-largest flat area, and the far west is many small valleys among hills.

bg-CLGi.title: Bollard: generic, red front reflector, rare
bg-CLGi.summary: Bollards are fairly rare. When seen, they are a generic design with a red reflector at the front and a white one at the back, and shape varies. Croatian and Hungarian bollards are fairly similar.

bg-Cs2I.title: Plate: standard EU, blue strip on left
bg-Cs2I.summary: The typical European plate design with a blue strip on the left.

bg-D7we.title: Sign: street word улица or ул.
bg-D7we.summary: The word for street is улица (ulitsa), sometimes shortened to ул. Older signs are more often Cyrillic only. Russia uses the same word.

bg-GRh6.title: Google car: invisible Gen 4 car
bg-GRh6.summary: Coverage where the Gen 4 car is completely hidden is found along the north and west borders and the northern half of the coast.

bg-IGYS.title: Sign: blue arrow direction signs
bg-IGYS.summary: Blue arrow-shaped direction signs with Cyrillic and Latin text. Even from far away you can see two lines of text instead of one.

bg-LaoB.title: Landscape: wind turbines near the coast
bg-LaoB.summary: Wind turbines are most common in the northeastern coastal province, usually towards the coast.

bg-Ml2y.title: Google car: white Gen 3, taped long antenna
bg-Ml2y.summary: Gen 3 coverage with a white car and a long antenna with tape, around one southern city and rarely on small roads elsewhere. This combination exists in other European countries too, so check other clues.

bg-QHMB.title: Rubbish bin: metal bin of this shape
bg-QHMB.summary: Metal rubbish bins of this shape are very common. Turkey, Serbia, Albania and North Macedonia use this style too.

bg-ZCSx.title: Sign: pedestrian crossing, four stripes, hat
bg-ZCSx.summary: A crossing sign with four stripes and a person wearing a hat. No other Eastern or Central European crossing sign has four stripes.

bg-bVxa.title: Google car: Gen 3, tape on a short antenna
bg-bVxa.summary: Older Gen 3 coverage with a piece of tape on a short antenna is common in the east. It rarely appears elsewhere, and is never found in four provinces.

bg-dPl7.title: Houses: old stone, white walls, brown wood
bg-dPl7.summary: Well-preserved old buildings of unpainted stone, white stone walls and brown wood, with cobblestone streets. Found in an old coastal town and to a lesser degree a nearby one.

bg-dsZv.title: Pole: small alternating hook insulators
bg-dsZv.summary: Most poles carry small insulators shaped like hooks, alternating from side to side. They also appear on wooden poles in some other countries, but on concrete poles it points to here.

bg-h4Uc.title: Houses: Alpine style, white walls, brown wood
bg-h4Uc.summary: Alpine-looking buildings with white walls and brown wooden details, common around the southern mountain region.

bg-hSvg.title: Pole: round concrete, sometimes ladder or wood
bg-hSvg.summary: Most poles are round and concrete. A rarer concrete ladder pole exists, and simple wooden poles show up now and then.

bg-kOSE.title: Road: poor quality, small cracks, potholes
bg-kOSE.summary: Roads are generally poor, with many small cracks and the occasional pothole.

bg-lm-104632.title: Houses: small, dense, poor suburbs
bg-lm-104632.summary: Suburbs are among the poorest in Europe, with small, densely built houses and a rough look.

bg-lm-740401.title: Sign: two street sign styles, one more common
bg-lm-740401.summary: Two different street sign designs are found in one southern city; the left one is more common.

bg-lskQ.title: Sign: plain white town entry, two text lines
bg-lskQ.summary: A simple white town entry sign with Cyrillic and Latin names. The two lines of text are visible even from afar.

bg-mr8t.title: Landscape: distinct bumpy mountains to the
bg-mr8t.summary: Mountains to the southwest of one northwestern town have a very distinct bumpy shape and are visible from far away.

bg-pclm.title: Google car: bulky antenna tip, unpeeled tape
bg-pclm.summary: An antenna with unpeeled tape on top makes the tip look bulkier. It is found in the northeastern province, always shot in March, so it looks dead and wintery.

bg-rCxW.title: Chevron: red on white
bg-rCxW.summary: Red arrows on white. Romania, Turkey and North Macedonia use the same chevrons, while Greece and Serbia use black and white ones.

differs.how: Greek chevrons are black and white
Serbian chevrons are black and white

bg-sB8m.title: Sign: brown street name, bright yellow text
bg-sB8m.summary: Brown street signs with bright yellow text, found in one southern city.

bg-vKm1.title: Google car: blue, red or black Gen 4
bg-vKm1.summary: Three newer Gen 4 cars: blue (most of Europe), red (also Latvia, Lithuania, Russia, Slovakia, Sweden) and black (many countries). Each can have an antenna or not, and sometimes the car is fully hidden.

differs.how: Russia and Slovakia are easiest to confuse for the red car
Greece and Croatia are easiest to confuse for the black car

bg-yVXY.title: Google car: grey tape on antenna tip
bg-yVXY.summary: A small piece of grey tape on top of the antenna in Gen 3 coverage (sometimes called a flag antenna). Not all Gen 3 has it. Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary and Romania have it too.

bg-yvT6.title: Landscape: tall pyramid-shaped peaks
bg-yvT6.summary: Towering mountains with tall pyramid-shaped peaks, seen from a few places in three provinces in the southwest.
